verdict.root_cause: Checkout's PlaceOrder fails during shipping-quote preparation: in all 10 sampled failing traces the only erroring child of PlaceOrder is checkout's own outbound HTTP POST to shipping's get-quote endpoint, while shipping's server-side span for that same call completes in 0.0-0.5ms with no error [tr_144a6c7eb049]. The failure is a fast non-2xx response, not a stall (1-13ms hop, whole trace under ~100ms), and the error propagates unchanged up through frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator, which explains why those three alerted simultaneously. The checkout root error text attributes the failure to a bad HTTP status from the email service, yet no email-service span appears anywhere in the traces [tr_144a6c7eb049] — so the failing status most plausibly originates behind or within the shipping quote path from a dependency that is answering with an error status rather than slowly. No change, metric or log evidence survives to pin a mechanism: checkout's change log is empty [tr_67b891fad93c], shipping's changes ended ~8.2h before onset on a net-zero revert [tr_487c5096137d], and both services' logs and shipping's span metrics are entirely empty across baseline and incident alike [tr_09b92440a2ac][tr_3266ccd76997][tr_d0e5acbb3108]. The mechanism is therefore unresolved; what is established is the failing hop and its location.
verdict.reasoning: Traces are the only signal with content and they are unanimous: 10/10 failing traces fail at the same hop, checkout->shipping get-quote, with error status propagating upward and every other checkout dependency (cart, Redis) succeeding and payment/currency/catalog never reached [tr_144a6c7eb049]. That localises the fault to the shipping quote path and rules out checkout's own handler, the frontend tiers, and a latency/timeout mechanism — the hop is milliseconds long, so dependency_latency, process_freeze and network_partition are all excluded by span duration. The mechanism behind the error status is not established. Shipping's server span is clean and short, which is consistent with shipping returning a well-formed error quickly, but shipping emits no logs and no span metrics in either window [tr_3266ccd76997][tr_d0e5acbb3108], so nothing distinguishes a misconfigured endpoint, a bad dependency response, or an application-level rejection. The change record argues against bad_deploy and bad_config as acts: shipping's image flapping ended ~8.2h before onset on a revert to the pre-burst value [tr_487c5096137d], and checkout has no recorded changes at all [tr_67b891fad93c]. The email-service reference in the error message is the single most informative unexplained detail and the highest-value next probe. Naming shipping rather than checkout because checkout's aggregate error ratio actually fell below baseline [tr_00f4f66624d9] and its spans carry the error only as a client-side record of a response it received.
open_questions: What HTTP status and body does shipping's get-quote actually return, and does it reference the email service? No shipping logs exist to answer this.
Why does checkout's error message name the email service when no email-service span appears in any trace — is email called synchronously without instrumentation, or is the message mislabeled?
Why are shipping's logs and span metrics empty across both the baseline and incident windows, and does that telemetry gap hide a shipping-side fault or merely reflect a collection/labeling problem?
What changed at 23:21:46 given no change record exists adjacent to onset for either checkout or shipping — was there an unrecorded flag flip or a change on an undispatched service such as email?

alternatives.root_cause: A runtime flag or unrecorded toggle on the shipping quote path turned on a code branch that returns an error status, which is why no artifact or config change appears in the change log.
alternatives.why_not: Purely inferred from the absence of change records; no flag store was queried and no shipping log or metric confirms a changed code path, so this is an explanation for silence rather than evidence of one.

alternatives.root_cause: The email service returns a bad HTTP status to the shipping quote path, and shipping propagates that status to checkout as a fast error.
alternatives.why_not: The checkout error message names email, but no email span appears in any of the 10 traces and no email dispatch was run, so the service was never observed; it is the most likely next lead, not a supported verdict.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any signal is expected. What should happen instead is investigation: capture the actual HTTP status and body checkout receives from shipping's get-quote (trace span attributes on the erroring client span, or a packet/proxy-level capture), and resolve why shipping emits neither logs nor span metrics while its server span appears in every trace. Until one of those returns a value, no permitted action has a mechanism to address.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if evidence surfaces that meets a precondition I judged unmet: a change record for checkout or shipping inside the incident window (none exists — checkout's log is empty and was queried forward from onset rather than backward [tr_67b891fad93c], and shipping's last change is ~8.2h before onset ending on a net-zero revert [tr_487c5096137d]), or an indication that the failure is process state rather than a deterministic non-2xx. The strongest contrary signal would be the failure clearing on its own or on an unrelated restart, which would suggest transient process state after all. It is also wrong if the right target is email — checkout's error text names it [tr_144a6c7eb049] — but email emits no span in any trace, so I have no evidence tying a permitted action to it, and acting on an uninstrumented guess is worse than waiting.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that the failure is persistent and every PlaceOrder keeps failing while nobody acts — a sustained, total checkout outage for the duration. I accept that over the alternative: a restart of shipping would be a guess (the evidence explicitly rules out shipping being slow or failing — its server span completes in 0.0-0.5ms with no error [tr_144a6c7eb049]), and a rollback or config revert on either service would fabricate a change-in-window that the change log says does not exist [tr_67b891fad93c][tr_487c5096137d]. A restart of shipping would also destroy the only live state that could still answer the open question of what status it returns.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. The existing blast radius persists: checkout fails, and the error propagates unchanged through frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator, which is why all four alerted together [tr_144a6c7eb049]. Had I proposed restarting shipping, checkout would have seen connection resets during the recreate on top of the errors it already returns.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical, simultaneous alerts across checkout, frontend and proxy with downstream load-generator impact indicate a real user-facing failure that cannot be dismissed. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the fan-out of checkout dependencies leaves the cause genuinely open.
